question: Would evaluator-selected cases expose a materially different failure profile from the author-selected public fixtures?
current_wall: Plectis publishes author-selected fixtures and one dated cold rerun, but no outside evaluator has selected a preregistered case set or published an independent failure taxonomy.

leading_hypothesis.statement: Evaluator-selected cases would expose more failures and a broader failure taxonomy than the current author-selected fixtures.

evidence_for.observation: The paper identifies author control over component, case, expectation, and pass-rule selection.
evidence_for.supports: Selection can hide difficult or unrepresentative cases even when every published run is repeatable.
evidence_for.authority_ceiling: This is an argument about possible selection effects, not a measured effect size.

evidence_for.observation: A cold public rerun found a real CLI-to-evaluator wiring defect that the normal author-controlled path had not exposed.
evidence_for.supports: A different inspection route can reveal a distinct failure mode.
evidence_for.authority_ceiling: One repaired defect does not estimate the frequency or severity of undiscovered defects.

evidence_against_or_missing.observation: No evaluator-controlled case corpus or outside report is currently available.
evidence_against_or_missing.supports: The leading hypothesis has no independent comparative sample.
evidence_against_or_missing.authority_ceiling: Absence of an outside report is not evidence that the public fixtures are representative or unrepresentative.

leading_hypothesis.would_be_displaced_by: A preregistered independent evaluation finding the same failure distribution, with enough coverage and a separately justified taxonomy, would displace the leading hypothesis.

alternatives.statement: The current public fixtures approximate the failure profile that evaluator-selected cases would reveal.
Most new failures would be environment or dependency failures rather than failures hidden by case selection.

discriminating_evidence.evidence_needed: An outside evaluator preregisters a sampling rule, selects cases without substitution, runs the pinned release, and publishes all outcomes.

result_map.result: Substantially more semantic or validator failures
A comparable failure profile under adequate coverage
result_map.interpretation: Supports approximate representativeness of the current fixtures.

discriminating_evidence.claim_ceiling: One evaluator and one release still do not establish representativeness of the private system.

discriminating_evidence.evidence_needed: Classify every independent failure using a taxonomy fixed before inspecting outcomes, separating semantic, validator, packaging, dependency, and environment failures.

result_map.interpretation: Supports the claim that author-selected cases missed substantive defects.

discriminating_evidence.claim_ceiling: The taxonomy measures the evaluated cases only and does not prove absence of other failure classes.

expert_return.request: Design or conduct an evaluator-controlled, preregistered public inspection that can distinguish selection effects from environment effects, and return the sampling rule, raw outcomes, and fixed failure taxonomy.

decisive_returns.requested_input: A public preregistration, exact release identity, complete case list, commands, raw outcomes, and taxonomy assignments.
decisive_returns.effect_if_verified: Adds independent evidence about the evaluated public release and updates the working hypothesis according to the declared discriminator.

route_only_returns.requested_input: An informal review or a small set of reviewer-chosen examples without preregistration.
route_only_returns.effect_if_verified: Can reveal concrete defects and improve routes, but cannot compare failure profiles under a controlled selection rule.
route_only_returns.claim_ceiling: It does not distinguish author-selection effects from reviewer-selection effects.
